scope: post-certification database-only hardening of legacy client-executable SECURITY DEFINER admin diagnostics that either ignored the declared admin session token or treated token presence/non-emptiness as authentication
classifier_scope: client-executable public SECURITY DEFINER functions with an argument named admin_session_token or admin_session_token_input; exact unused-token plus weak presence/nonempty patterns, excluding known validating/delegating guard owners and possession-semantic admin_logout
notes: The functions remain browser-callable under their pre-existing ACLs, but SECURITY DEFINER diagnostic access now requires the already-declared admin session token to validate.
No active admin token, JWT, push subscription endpoint, push auth/DH material, or other secret is stored in this proof artifact.

The first attempted 20260830001727 migration submission was rejected transactionally by PostgreSQL for a syntax error before any function was changed; the corrected migration was then applied successfully under version 20260830001727.

A follow-on exact ignored-parameter classifier found three additional home/profile diagnostics v685-v687; migration 20260830002126 hardened those three and the same classifier then returned zero rows.

CI for the first two migrations was revalidated against main 40c7329b22182c7fe627afa8c4c24490bcfab3e0 after PR #309 repaired an unrelated Bruis shop Pages-boundary checker regression without relaxing the global JSON publication exclusion.

The broader guard-family sweep then found seven diagnostics that used only token presence/non-emptiness rather than session validity. Migration 20260830100535 added the canonical guard to those seven; 7/7 anonymous NULL calls now reject, v650 also rejects a non-empty invalid token, and the weak-auth classifier returns zero rows.
admin_logout is intentionally not classified as weak auth: possession of the supplied token identifies only the session row to revoke, and an invalid token deletes nothing.
